activity_context.topic_title: Cumulative Distribution Functions for Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(4<X\le 6).$

| $x$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $0.9$ | $1.0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $X$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a<X\le b)=F(b)-F(a).
$$

Here, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4<X\le 6) & =F(6)-F(4) \\  & =0.9-0.4 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$
